elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.6 states that Customer shall pay no liquidated damages under the Agreement.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.6 states that Customer shall pay no penalties under the Agreement.

elements.element: A liquidated amount may be payable by Customer only if triggered by early termination.
elements.evidence: The clause categorically prohibits all liquidated damages payable by Customer, so no liquidated amount can arise outside the permitted early-termination circumstance.

elements.element: Any early-termination liquidated amount payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause permits no early-termination liquidated amount at all; therefore, no amount can exceed the three-month cap.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The broader prohibition on all liquidated damages ensures that no other liquidated amount is payable by Customer.

result.reason: The operative redline fully implements the preferred position by replacing the USD 25,000-per-day liquidated-damages obligation with an agreement-wide prohibition on liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. This more protective prohibition also satisfies the fallback constraints because no early-termination fee or other liquidated amount can arise. The change does not waive or restrict Vendor's ordinary, non-liquidated remedies.
